name: LiveKit Agent Session Archive
purpose: Record LiveKit voice-agent sessions through Egress directly to Backblaze B2, link each recording to its transcription and evaluation in a per-session manifest, and apply retention by session class.
tagline: LiveKit Egress recordings, manifests and retention on Backblaze B2.

features.title: Session Recording
features.summary: create a room, dispatch the test agent, and have Egress record it straight to B2

features.title: Session Library
features.summary: browse sessions under sessions/, play recordings, edit class or label, reprocess, delete

features.title: Webhook Manifests
features.summary: verified LiveKit webhooks, stored as evidence, keep each session manifest current

features.title: Transcription and Evaluation
features.summary: local faster-whisper transcript, word error rate and expected-phrase check

features.title: Retention
features.summary: keep or remove sessions by class, with a per-day report in B2

features.title: File Browser
features.summary: list, preview, download, delete any object in the bucket

features.title: Dashboard
features.summary: sessions by class and status, recorded minutes and bytes, last retention run

features.title: Settings
features.summary: theme plus labelled demo preference fields

b2_surface.why: LiveKit Egress's own S3 uploader writes sessions/<date>/<room>/recording.ogg directly to B2; the API never re-uploads it
manifest.json, transcript.json, evaluation.json, webhooks/<event_id>.json and reports/<date>.json
SHA-256 of the recording, transcription input, and reading manifests and reports
recording size and ETag, checked against the webhook's size; the /api/health probe
session list (manifests under sessions/), reports list, and the full-bucket explorer
retention and session delete remove every version, so the bytes are actually gone
audio playback and downloads in the UI

stack.web: Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query, livekit-client
stack.storage: Backblaze B2 (S3-compatible API), written directly by LiveKit Egress

env_vars.name: B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID
env_vars.note: B2 application key ID (**keyID** in the B2 console); the API passes it to Egress per request

env_vars.name: B2_APPLICATION_KEY
env_vars.note: B2 application key (**applicationKey**), shown once at creation

env_vars.name: B2_BUCKET_NAME
env_vars.note: bucket unique name (**Bucket Unique Name** in the B2 console)

env_vars.name: B2_REGION
env_vars.note: the region inside the bucket's **Endpoint** (`s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com`); the S3 endpoint for boto3 and Egress is derived from it

env_vars.name: B2_PUBLIC_URL_BASE
env_vars.note: public object base URL, when the bucket is public

env_vars.name: LIVEKIT_API_KEY
env_vars.note: local LiveKit dev key shared by the server, Egress, the agent and the API; any placeholder works locally

env_vars.name: LIVEKIT_API_SECRET
env_vars.note: local LiveKit dev secret (at least 32 characters); signs room tokens and webhooks

env_vars.name: LIVEKIT_URL
env_vars.note: where the API reaches LiveKit inside Compose (default `ws://livekit:7880`)

env_vars.name: LIVEKIT_PUBLIC_URL
env_vars.note: where a browser on the host reaches LiveKit (default `ws://localhost:7880`)

env_vars.name: ARCHIVE_PREFIX
env_vars.note: prefix for every key this app writes (default empty; `make test` uses `e2e/<run-id>/`)

env_vars.name: EVAL_MAX_WER
env_vars.note: highest word error rate that still passes (default 0.5)

env_vars.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
env_vars.note: API origin for the web UI (default `http://localhost:8000`); Next.js inlines it at build time
